newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian entrepreneur snaps up Banco Popular.
newsitem.headline: Colombian entrepreneur snaps up Banco Popular.

text.p: One of Colombia's top entrepreneurs, Luis Carlos Sarmiento Angulo, snapped up an 80 percent stake in state-run Banco Popular for 271.9 billion pesos to consolidate his position as the country's largest individual banker.

Sarmiento's was the only bid for the country's seventh largest bank in terms of assets, which in the nine-months to September posted 20.3 billion pesos net profits, a 133 percent rise against the same period last year, with total assets of 1.5 trillion pesos.

The privatization was the biggest in Colombia this year. The 80 percent stake comprised 4.48 billion shares valued at 60.6 pesos each. The auction was conducted simultaneously through the bourses in Bogota, Medellin and Cali after the end of normal trading.

In a parallel auction a further 13.3 percent was put up for sale, but only 0.11 percent was actually bought, by a brokerage firm Valores del Popular. The rest of that packet is likely to be bought in normal stock exchange trading in the coming weeks. The remaining 6.7 percent stake in Banco Popular is in the hands of local governments across Colombia.
Sarmiento bought his controlling stake through his holding company Popular Investment, according to Francisco Azuero, head of Colombia's state-run privatization committee Fogafin.

Colombia's leading daily El Tiempo said the deal was financed using profits from the sale of Cementos Samper to Mexican cement producer Cemex earlier this year and with a loan from the Bank of America.

The financier already controls Banco de Bogota, Colombia's fourth largest bank in terms of assets, Banco Occidente, the ninth largest bank, and has controlling stakes in savings banks, building societies and financial corporations.

The move makes him the single biggest banker in Colombia. But he will be taking on a bank in dispute. The Banco Popular union has called a strike starting Friday morning to protest against the privatization process.
Despite the moderate growth of the Colombian economy, forecast to end the year around 3.5 percent, the banking sector has remained buoyant.

Investment consultants Santander Investment said in its October report: "The Colombian banking sector remains highly profitable. In the first half of 1996, consolidated net profits for the sector rose by 24 percent year to year in real terms."
